propositions: The axis `divergent_implementation` is mis-calibrated with an ordinal `none|low|medium|high` ladder, fires on only 7.72% of plan-v3 findings, and has never been calibrated with worked examples or a closed literal set, unlike its sibling `ac_unverifiable`.

A G6 finding (fc347224733dccc6b) scored `impact=0.0` and landed ADVISORY despite `validity=0.8889` and `blocking_enabled=true` because all seven impact axes graded `none`; the real harm was expressed in superseded mean-model axes (`prod_impact: medium`, `blast_radius: module`), not in the MAX model's inputs.

The axis must be re-graded as a closed Literal with three kinds: `contradicts_reality` and `omits_required_site` (hard floor 0.85), and `incomplete_enumeration` (below all blocking thresholds, never floors), mirroring the `ac_unverifiable` oracle-kind precedent exactly.

The structural change to `impact_plan` must exclude `divergent_implementation` from the generic `_SEV01` loop and add `DIVERGENCE_GRADE01` mapping, introducing `_PLAN_GRADED_AXES` to unify both kind-graded axes and prevent drift.

Purpose-built LLM eval suites and bulk re-review runs must be rejected as calibration instruments; only corpus replay (offline re-scoring the existing corpus under candidate values) and dogfooding (observing field results) are permitted, to minimize cost and avoid non-terminating feedback loops.

Every prompt-side consumer (`plan_review_verifier.md`, `plan_review_verifier_agentic.md`, `plan_review_G7.md`) and fixture (`tests/unit/test_a8e5_operator_attested_edge.py`, `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py:1282`) must be migrated to the closed Literal; the ordinal grades are parse errors under the new type.
